title: A 10-Foot Worm Hides in Sand and Slices Fish in Half

scenes.text: Something buried in this sand cuts fish in half.
It's the bobbit worm, up to ten feet long, hidden with only its antennae showing.
A curious fish swims close to check them out.
Then the worm lunges out like a coiled spring, and its scissor-like jaws snap shut.
It can slice a fish clean in half and drag it underground.
Next time you see calm sand underwater, remember what might be waiting.

description:
Something buried in this sand cuts fish in half.
The bobbit worm grows up to ten feet long and waits in the seafloor with only its antennae showing. When a fish comes close, it lunges out and snaps its serrated jaws shut.
Would you swim over this sand? Tell us below.
first_comment: The bobbit worm is almost blind. It finds fish with antennae that sense light and chemicals. Would you dive here?
